Procedures performed: Compared invoice totals with general ledger postings and bank deposits, checked invoice dates and quantities against available bills of lading, and reviewed the customer hold request and warehouse segregation note for the bill-and-hold item.

Samples tested: [[item:INV-1002]], [[item:INV-1009]], [[item:INV-1015]], [[item:INV-1020]], [[item:INV-1026]], [[item:INV-1028]], [[item:INV-1039]], [[item:INV-1066]], [[item:INV-1079]], [[item:INV-1092]], [[item:INV-1110]], [[item:INV-1112]], [[item:INV-1113]], [[item:INV-1114]], [[item:INV-1115]], [[item:INV-1116]], [[item:INV-1117]], [[item:INV-1118]], [[item:INV-1119]], [[item:INV-1120]], and [[item:INV-1121]].

Results: For the eighteen samples without exceptions, invoice totals agreed with ledger postings and bank deposits, shipped quantities agreed with invoiced quantities, and shipment and invoicing fell in the same reporting period.

Exceptions:
- [[item:INV-1015]]: The ledger posting agreed with the invoice, but no bill of lading or matching bank statement entry was provided. The ledger match does not establish shipment or its timing.
- [[item:INV-1026]]: The ledger posting was below the invoice total of [[ev:ev-INV-1026-invoice_amount]]. The bank deposit agreed with the invoice total.
- [[item:INV-1110]]: The ledger posting and bank deposit agreed with the invoice. No bill of lading was provided. The customer requested a hold until [[ev:ev-INV-1110-hold_until_date]], and the warehouse note showed that all invoiced units were segregated. The evidence did not establish a substantive reason for the hold, readiness for transfer at year-end, or that the seller could not redirect the goods. Recognition in the year under audit was therefore not supported.

Conclusion: No exceptions were noted for the remaining samples. Obtain alternative shipment and collection evidence, reconcile the ledger difference, and assess whether a revenue cutoff adjustment is needed before closing the test.
